neighbours.label: nutrient and toxin chemistry in water-quality text: the link words between pollutant terms ('nitrogen and phosphorus', 'algae release toxins', 'ammonia to nitrite')
fire: Fertilizer runoff carries nitrates and phosphates into the reservoir.
Blooms of blue-green algae can produce toxins that poison livestock.
Excess phosphorus in the pond feeds the growth of cyanobacteria.
Wastewater plants remove ammonia and nitrogen before discharge.
Some diatoms release domoic acid, a toxin that harms shellfish eaters.
Elevated nitrate concentrations in well water endanger infants.
Farm effluent raises the levels of nitrogen and potassium in the creek.
Nitrifying bacteria oxidize ammonium into nitrate in the aquarium filter.
quiet: Spring floods carry branches and gravel into the reservoir.
Blooms of water lilies can cover the pond by late summer.
Cold water in the pond slows the growth of the goldfish.
Wastewater plants screen out sticks and plastic before discharge.
Some ducks raise their young along the shellfish beds.
Low water levels in the well worry the farmers in July.
Heavy rain raises the level of the creek by several feet.
A small pump moves water through the aquarium filter.

notes: Card: peaks on 'and' (nitrogen and phosphorus), 'called' (purines), 'release' (algae release toxins), 'nit'(rate), plus an off-topic 'International' in CC license lines. Probe: nutrient/algae sentences 0.39-0.48; plain river sentence 0.01; CC license line 0.88 (a second trigger, not tested here). Near misses are water topics without nutrient/toxin chemistry.
